description: INS, the national statistics institute of Niger, publishes the analysis reports of the 2012 General Population and Housing Census on its census page, and one report covers housing characteristics and the living environment. Its tables count dwellings by type and tenure, and by dominant wall material from banco earth and straw through semi-permanent and permanent construction, with roof tables alongside, split by urban and rural area. Chapter four covers households by cooking energy, lighting mode (grid electricity, own electricity, battery lamps), drinking water supply, household waste disposal and toilet type, with lighting shown by region, and an equipment table by region. An indicator page gives headline shares, for example that in towns grid electricity is the main lighting source for 53 percent of households. Coverage is national. Format and access: free PDF, no registration. Licence: the INS open data licence allows commercial and non-commercial reuse with attribution. Caveats: data date from 2012, most tables split only urban and rural, not region or commune, and the ANADO microdata catalogue did not list the 2012 census when searched. Simulation uses: building material shares for flood and heat exposure, and grid versus battery lighting for electrification planning. Related records: the WorldPop GRID3 census-based population grids.
